extensions.category: Stable error category derived from top-level code (required).
extensions.code: Top-level stable error code from registry.top_level_codes[].code (required).
extensions.debug_ref: Optional safe opaque reference for support (never a stack trace).
extensions.errors: Optional list of field-level errors for validation failures.
extensions.occurred_at: RFC3339/ISO8601 UTC timestamp string with microsecond precision (6 fractional digits).
extensions.request_id: Required correlation identifier (must be propagated end-to-end).
extensions.retry_after_seconds: If retryable, optionally provide suggested backoff (seconds).
extensions.trace_id: Optional distributed tracing identifier (W3C traceparent/trace-id source).

ERR-INV-TIME-USEC.text: All occurred_at timestamps in error envelopes MUST use utc_datetime_usec (microsecond precision).

aggregate_translation_rules: If the raised/returned error is an aggregate with an `errors` collection, the translator MUST examine all underlying errors.
If any underlying error is Forbidden, the top-level code MUST be ERR_FORBIDDEN unless a more specific top-level code is explicitly mandated by a domain contract.
If any underlying error is Invalid and none are Forbidden, the top-level code MUST be ERR_VALIDATION.
If none match known classes, fallback MUST be ERR_INTERNAL.
Underlying errors MAY be mapped into `errors[]` for validation-style payloads only when safe.

rules: Application code MUST NOT use `authorize?: false` for external callers.
System-actor internal flows MAY bypass authorization only with explicit justification and audit logging.
All bypass usage MUST map forbidden/unauthorized outcomes to ERR_FORBIDDEN/ERR_UNAUTHENTICATED and MUST NOT leak policy internals.

notes: Ash may return a single exception that aggregates multiple underlying errors; the aggregate exception includes an `errors` key containing the underlying errors.
Translation MUST preserve the most user-relevant classification (e.g., Forbidden vs Invalid) while retaining underlying errors for logging/diagnostics.

Ash translation produces the internal classification and causal subcode. It does not by itself define the HTTP response. Before serializing a tenant-scoped HTTP error, the boundary MUST apply mappings.tenant_hidden_http_boundary; TEN-1 externalization takes precedence over the Ash classification.
translation_algorithm: Implementations MUST first normalize any thrown/returned value to an Ash exception container (e.g., via Ash.Error.to_ash_error/3) before mapping to ERR-1 codes.
Implementations MUST inspect the exception container's nested `errors` (if present) to derive a more specific top-level code/subcode; container class alone is insufficient.
If any nested error is Ash.Error.Query.NotFound, implementations MUST map to top-level ERR_NOT_FOUND (subcode optional).
If any nested error is Ash.Error.Invalid.Timeout, implementations MUST map to top-level ERR_TIMEOUT (subcode optional).
If any nested error is Ash.Error.Invalid.TenantRequired, implementations MUST map to top-level ERR_FORBIDDEN with subcode TEN_TENANT_CONTEXT_MISSING.

The Ash classification and subcode for Ash.Error.Invalid.TenantRequired are internal diagnostic context. Before emitting an HTTP response for missing tenant context, implementations MUST apply mappings.tenant_hidden_http_boundary and MUST NOT serialize the internal classification or cause subcode.

notes: IR-prefixed subcodes are internal/operator truth and MUST NOT be leaked raw to public clients.
Public boundaries MUST map IR-prefixed containment outcomes to generic top-level classes and user-safe messages while preserving correlation_id for support and observability.

rules: Oban job errors MUST be classified using ERR-1 codes to ensure consistent alerting and retry strategy.
Retry decisions MUST align with retryability taxonomy; job configuration may override with stricter behavior.
Webhook delivery failures MUST be recorded with stable code/subcode and retryability.
Webhook consumers MUST receive the canonical problem-details envelope on webhook error callbacks (if implemented).

tenant_hidden_http_boundary.precedence: Apply before HTTP serialization for every applies_to case. TEN-1 external response policy overrides Ash classification and ERR-1 registry top-level mappings. Preserve internal classifications and causes for audit and telemetry only. TEN_SUPPORT_MODE_UNAUTHORIZED remains ERR_FORBIDDEN and is not a tenant-hidden case under this mapping.

rules: Field errors MUST be safe to show to end-users.
Field errors MUST NOT contain secrets, raw SQL, stack traces, or internal IDs not intended for the caller.

notes: `type` MUST be a stable URI identifying the problem type (no secrets; no request-specific data).
`instance` MUST be the request path or a stable request identifier suitable for support correlation.
`detail` MUST be safe for the caller. Internal diagnostics MUST go to logs/traces and be referenced via request_id/trace_id/debug_ref.

must_not_expose: Passwords, secrets, tokens, API keys, private keys
Raw stack traces in client responses
Raw SQL queries or database connection details
PII beyond what the caller already provided (e.g., full ID numbers, payment PAN, CVV)
Internal IDs that are not contractually allowed to be exposed
rules: Client-facing `detail` MUST be safe-by-default and free of internal diagnostics.
If a client needs more detail, the mechanism MUST be support correlation via request_id/trace_id/debug_ref, not richer error bodies.

invariants: Every subcode MUST reference an existing top-level code.
Top-level codes MUST be stable; rename is forbidden. Deprecation requires keeping old codes as deprecated aliases only if explicitly allowed.
Subcodes MUST NOT begin with 'ERR_' (reserved for top-level codes).
New codes/subcodes require test-gate updates and CANON pin updates.
Subcodes MUST include a domain prefix + at least one underscore separator (e.g., ORD_*, EVT_*, TEN_*).

subcodes.notes: Session or grant assurance epoch is stale due to MFA/security posture change. Client MUST re-authenticate and re-verify strong step-up as required.
Consumer proof (IAM-2: sms/email OTP, consumer passkeys) is insufficient for this capability. Requires IAM-3 strong step-up (aal2_strong).
Recovery code usage MUST emit ticketing.iam.mfa.recovery_used security signal and require AAL2 re-enrollment for privileged actions.
One or more add-on line items reference a base line item that is not present in the order payload or is not eligible.
Order checkout attempt is outside the allowed checkout TTL window; client MUST restart checkout and obtain fresh price snapshot / holds.
entitlement_allocations is missing required fields, has invalid types, references unknown line_key, or violates allocation invariants (e.g., mixed entitlement_kind within one line_key).
Sum(qty) of entitlement_allocations per line_key MUST equal the signed priced line quantity; mismatch indicates drift between requested allocations and signed PRICE snapshot.
Payment capture/settlement confirmed after the associated seat hold expired; system MUST NOT issue entitlements and MUST attempt provider void or refund deterministically.
Subscriber-priced lines MUST NOT stack with promo/coupon/other discounts. Raised when discount_stack_kind != "none" or discount_total_minor != 0 while entitlement context is present.
Generic public-facing containment block when incident posture is active; public boundaries MUST NOT leak internal scope or tier labels.
Used when a scoped incident containment blocks the attempted operation.
Used when incident posture forces stronger proof or recent re-verification before proceeding.

client_rules: Clients MUST treat retryable=true as a hint, not a guarantee.
Clients MUST respect `Retry-After` if present (HTTP) or retry_after_seconds in body.
Retries MUST be idempotent; if not idempotent, client MUST use idempotency keys or avoid automatic retry.

taxonomy.meaning: Client MUST NOT retry automatically; fix request or permissions.
taxonomy.name: never

taxonomy.meaning: Client MAY retry only when the request is safe to retry (idempotent) and conditions indicate a transient failure; generally used for conflicts or transient upstream errors.
taxonomy.name: conditional

taxonomy.meaning: Client MUST retry with exponential backoff and jitter; used for timeouts, rate limiting, and temporary unavailability.
taxonomy.name: always

rules.rationale: Prevents integrity drift and makes canon pinning meaningful.
rules.text: ERR-1 contract and ERR-1-GATE MUST be the only normative sources for error envelope shape and error code registry. Filenames MUST match the CS-0 bundle conventions; repack suffixes (_rN) are forbidden.

rules.rationale: Standardized error shape improves client handling and observability.
rules.text: All HTTP API errors MUST be emitted as RFC9457 Problem Details (application/problem+json) and MUST include all fields in problem_details.required_fields. Only problem_details.optional_fields may be included as extensions.

rules.rationale: Registry integrity prevents freelancing and ambiguous error interpretation.
rules.text: Top-level codes and subcodes MUST be unique. Each subcode MUST reference an existing top-level code. Top-level codes MUST match registry.format_rules.top_level_code_pattern. Subcodes MUST match registry.format_rules.subcode_pattern.

rules.rationale: Prevents data leakage and reduces attack surface.
rules.text: Client-facing error payloads MUST NOT expose secrets, stack traces, raw SQL, or sensitive internal diagnostics. Use request_id/trace_id/debug_ref for support correlation. Redaction rules in redaction.must_not_expose are mandatory.

rules.rationale: Ash aggregates errors and returns structured exceptions; translation must be consistent across boundaries.
rules.text: Ash 3.x errors MUST be translated via mappings.mappings.ash_3. Translation MUST handle aggregates and MUST preserve the correct top-level classification while avoiding leakage of internal exception details.

rules.rationale: Prevents attackers from learning internal containment posture from client-facing error labels.
rules.text: IR-prefixed subcodes MUST be translated through mappings.incident_response_boundary at public boundaries. Raw IR-prefixed subcodes MUST remain internal to logs, traces, incident evidence, and privileged operator views.

rules.rationale: Ensures incident-response error vocabulary exists before implementation and remains deterministic across surfaces.
rules.text: Containment blocks, quarantine paths, severance gates, interactive-upgrade denial, leased-job barriers, and payout freezes triggered by incident posture MUST use registered IR-prefixed subcodes from ERR-1.registry.subcodes.

rules.rationale: Separates operator truth from user-safe messaging while preserving support correlation.
rules.text: Client-facing responses MAY expose only top-level code, user-safe message, correlation_id, and allowed extensions. Internal subcode, incident_id, approved_scope, and containment class are privileged details unless an explicit privileged boundary contract allows them.

summary: Canonical, enforceable error envelope + stable error code registry with incident-response vocabulary, public/internal boundary mapping, and CS-0@2.3.0 alignment.
title: ERR-1 — Error Handling & Error Code Registry

approved_authority_corrections.external_error_authority: ERR-1 alone defines external top-level error and subcode identifiers. Other contracts may reference registered ERR-1 identifiers only. Missing tenant and missing or wrong-tenant hidden resource responses are HTTP 404 ERR_NOT_FOUND; internal causes remain audit/telemetry only.
